options.then: The fight leaves everyone hurt and you more alone.

options.text: Lean on the people you trust, and keep Tele-MANAS 14416 handy
options.then: The tense evenings feel less lonely. You keep a steady routine.

steps.why: A wider circle can hold what home can't, and needing it is never your fault.

scenarios.debrief: When home can't hold all of you, a wider network holds the rest.
scenarios.relearn: You don't have to do adulthood alone; support comes from many places.

scenarios.hook: You want to tell someone you're struggling, but the thought of being a burden stops you.

steps.prompt: You type a message to your friend Neel, then stop at "I'll be a burden." What do you do?

options.text: Save it as a draft and wait for a better time
options.then: The better time doesn't come. The draft sits there.

options.text: Delete it and send a meme instead
options.then: He sends a laughing emoji back. The real message stays unsent.

options.text: Send it anyway, and let Neel choose how to respond
options.then: Neel replies within a minute: "Glad you told me. Call?"

options.text: Send a shorter version: "Tired lately, ignore this"
options.then: He says "Rest up!" Whatever you meant stays unsaid.

steps.why: Letting someone choose to show up is kinder to both of you than deciding for them.

steps.prompt: Later Neel says he has noticed you seem off and that you can always lean on him. He asks what would help. What do you say?

options.text: Say you'll tell him if it gets worse
options.then: He nods. You wait for "worse" and carry on alone.

options.text: Say a short call each evening would help for now
options.then: He answers, "Done. Evenings are yours."

options.text: Say you'd rather not take up his time
options.then: He frowns. "You wouldn't be."

options.text: Say nothing is needed, and you're fine
options.then: Neel says okay, but he looks unsure.

steps.why: Asking for something specific gives a caring friend a real way to help.

steps.prompt: Neel adds that other people care too, like your mother or a teacher. What do you do?

options.text: Ask Neel to tell them for you, so you never have to say it
options.then: Neel hesitates. "I'd rather stand next to you while you tell them."

options.text: Tell a trusted adult too, and let Neel stay close
options.then: Your mother holds you when you tell her. She says it plainly: "You are never a burden."

options.text: Tell your mother a smaller version, so she won't worry
options.then: She hugs you and says to rest up. The heavy part stays unsaid.

options.text: Decide Neel is enough, so you don't need anyone else
options.then: It works for a week. Neel gets tired, and you feel guilty.

steps.why: More than one supporter is safer for everyone, and you are not a burden.

scenarios.debrief: 'I'll be a burden' is a thought, not a fact; caring people want to be there.
scenarios.relearn: Reach out when struggling; you're not a burden to people who care.

scenarios.hook: It's a brutal stretch, and you've cut sleep, meals and friends to "push through."

steps.prompt: It's the third night of studying until 3 a.m. and skipping dinner. What do you do?

options.text: Cut only sleep, since meals take too long to make now
options.then: You gain two hours. You lose most of what you studied.

options.text: Rely on chai and energy drinks to keep yourself going
options.then: You stay awake, and the crash hits you in class.

options.text: Keep cutting everything so you can grind even harder
options.then: By morning your head is foggy, and you read the same page twice.

options.text: Put back the basics: sleep, food and a friend
options.then: You get a full night's sleep and eat. Your focus is better next day.

steps.why: You can't cope well on empty, so basics are fuel and not a luxury.

steps.prompt: Your friend Zoya messages that she misses your chats. What do you do?

options.text: Ignore it, so you don't lose study time
options.then: Her message sits unread. You feel a bit lonelier.

options.text: Say you'll catch up after the exams
options.then: She replies "okay!" and her message stays on your mind.

options.text: Meet her for ten minutes at break
options.then: You laugh for the first time in days. You go back to your books lighter.

options.text: Reply with a meme and nothing else
options.then: She sends a laughing face. It's not the same.

steps.why: A short break with a friend refuels you and keeps the connection alive.

steps.prompt: A teacher notices you look exhausted and says rest is part of revision. What do you do?

options.text: Nod politely, then keep following the same old schedule
options.then: The teacher's words fade by evening. The grind continues.

options.text: Say you'll rest properly after the exams are all over
options.then: The exams arrive. You are still running on empty.

options.text: Cut sleep only on the nights just before your tests
options.then: The nights before tests are the worst. You blank on a question.

options.text: Plan short breaks and a fixed bedtime
options.then: The next week feels steadier. You finish more in less time.

steps.why: Rest and routine keep your mind sharp, and they are part of the plan.

scenarios.debrief: Cutting self-care to push through backfires; basics let you keep going.
scenarios.relearn: Self-care basics like sleep and connection keep you able to cope.

scenarios.hook: You finally want to talk to someone, but you don't know how to start.

steps.prompt: You want to talk to your mother about how things have been. What do you do?

options.text: Write a long speech and rehearse it for days
options.then: The speech grows. Each day it gets harder to say.

options.text: Wait for the perfect moment to bring it up
options.then: There is always something else going on. The moment never arrives.

options.text: Say: "I've been having a hard time. Can we talk?"
options.then: She sits beside you. "Of course. I'm listening."

options.text: Drop vague hints and hope she figures it out
options.then: She asks if you're hungry. The hint passes her by.

steps.why: A plain, honest opener is enough, because you don't need perfect words.

steps.prompt: Later your mother gently asks what's on your mind. It's still hard to put into words. What do you do?

options.text: Say "never mind" and wait for the next time
options.then: She says okay and lets it drop. The weight grows.

options.text: Say you lack the words, but want her to listen
options.then: She nods. "Then say it however it comes."

options.text: Say it's nothing at all and change the subject
options.then: She lets it go. The unsaid thing stays.

options.text: Say it is just school stress, though it is more than that
options.then: She offers to help with studying. The real thing stays unsaid.

steps.why: Saying you can't find the words is enough to start.

steps.prompt: A few days on, your mother still looks worried. She says a counsellor might help too. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes, and ask her to come along to the first visit
options.then: She smiles. "I'll come. We'll go together."

options.text: Say you don't need one, and your family is enough
options.then: She nods. The heaviness has nowhere else to go.

options.text: Say you'll think about it, then let it slide
options.then: A month passes. The idea stays in a drawer.

options.text: Say counsellors are for people who can't cope
options.then: She answers gently: "They are for people who care about themselves."

steps.why: Pairing a trusted adult with a counsellor gives you the right level of help.

scenarios.debrief: You don't need perfect words; a simple, honest opener is enough.
scenarios.relearn: A simple, direct 'I could use someone to talk to' opens real support.

scenarios.hook: Your uncle's "help" is really pressure to follow his timeline for your life.

steps.prompt: Uncle says he's chosen your course and is only helping. What do you do?

options.text: Thank him, and say you'll decide by your own goals
options.then: He frowns, then says, "We'll see."

options.text: Agree, since he's helping so much
options.then: He beams. A small part of you sinks.

options.text: Nod politely, then plan to do something different in secret
options.then: Uncle thinks it's settled. The secret grows heavier.

options.text: Tell him loudly that he has no right to say anything
options.then: The room goes cold. Your mother looks worried.

steps.why: Thanking him and holding your own goals keeps the relationship and your choices.

steps.prompt: A teacher, Mrs. Das, offers to talk through your interests and options. What do you do?

options.text: Decline, since you don't want more opinions
options.then: She says the offer stands. You decide alone, without facts.

options.text: Accept, but let her choose for you
options.then: She suggests a course. It still isn't your choice.

options.text: Accept, and bring your own list of interests
options.then: Mrs. Das reads the list. "Good. Let's start with what you like."

options.text: Say Uncle already decided, so there's no need
options.then: She nods. The question stays unanswered.

steps.why: Facts and your own interests make a decision yours.

steps.prompt: Your mother says: "Uncle means well. What do you want?"

options.text: Say you don't know and don't care anymore
options.then: She sighs. Neither of you says more.

options.text: Say nobody understands you at all
options.then: She looks hurt. "I'm trying to."

options.text: Share your goals, and ask her to back you with Uncle
options.then: She smiles. "Okay. We'll talk to him together."

options.text: Say whatever Uncle says is fine
options.then: She searches your face. "Are you sure?"

steps.why: Real support listens to your goals and stands with you.

scenarios.debrief: Not all 'help' is support; the people who back your choices are your network.
scenarios.relearn: Your real support backs your own values, not someone else's timeline.

scenarios.hook: You are turning 18 soon, and you feel you should stop needing to lean on anyone.

steps.prompt: It's a week before your birthday, and a cousin offers to help with a big college choice. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, then tell everyone you did it alone
options.then: The cousin smiles tightly. You feel a little false.

options.text: Decline, to prove you're already an adult
options.then: You feel proud. The choice stays tangled.

options.text: Say you'll ask for help only after you turn 18
options.then: Birthday cake arrives. The choice is still unmade.

options.text: Accept, because adults ask for help too
options.then: She sits down with you. "Let's list your options."

steps.why: Adults ask for help all the time, and accepting it is a strength.

steps.prompt: After your birthday a friend says: "Now you're an adult. You should have it all figured out." What do you say?

options.text: Say you need nobody's help from now on
options.then: The friend shrugs. You feel proud, and also tired.

options.text: Laugh it off and hide that you feel lost
options.then: The friend laughs too. You feel a little more alone.

options.text: Say adults lean on people for life, and so do you
options.then: The friend thinks. "Huh. That's actually fair."

options.text: Agree, and stop asking for advice
options.then: You feel the pressure grow.

steps.why: Needing support doesn't end at 18, and everyone you admire still leans on people.

steps.prompt: A tough week hits, and your mother asks if she can help. What do you do?

options.text: Say yes, but give her no details
options.then: She hovers, unsure. You get less help than you could.

options.text: Say you'll manage because you're eighteen now
options.then: She nods. She seems a bit sad.

options.text: Say you'd rather not worry her
options.then: She says you could never worry her. You keep quiet anyway.

options.text: Say yes and tell her what would help
options.then: She makes tea and listens. The week feels shorter.

steps.why: Leaning on people you trust is how adults get through hard weeks.

scenarios.debrief: Turning 18 doesn't end your need for people; it's a need that lasts a lifetime.
scenarios.relearn: Needing support never expires; it continues for life.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Asha tells you she has thoughts that scare her.

steps.prompt: Asha says she's afraid to say more. What do you do?

options.text: Ask for every detail right now, so you can judge how bad it is
options.then: She feels questioned and says even less.

options.text: Change the subject to something lighter so she feels better soon
options.then: She laughs a little. The frightening thing goes unsaid again.

options.text: Tell her she's being a bit dramatic and should relax now
options.then: Asha shuts down. "Forget it."

options.text: Stay calm and say you're glad she told you
options.then: Her shoulders loosen. "I thought you'd think I was weird."

steps.why: Believing her and staying calm tells her she is safe to tell you, and it's not her fault.

steps.prompt: Later Asha asks: "Promise you'll keep this just between us." What do you do?

options.text: Promise, then tell her to try and just sleep it off tonight
options.then: She nods. The thoughts are still there.

options.text: Promise, and handle it all just between the two of you
options.then: You carry it together. It feels heavier each day.

options.text: Say you'll tell the whole class so that everyone can help her
options.then: Asha goes pale and asks you to stop. She is hurt, but stays beside you.

options.text: Say you can't keep it secret, and you'll stay with her
options.then: She cries a little. "Okay. I'm scared, but okay."

steps.why: Staying with her while more help joins keeps her safe, and none of this is her fault.

steps.prompt: Asha asks who she could tell. What do you do?

options.text: Say you'll figure it all out and tell her tomorrow instead
options.then: She waits, hopeful. You don't have an answer.

options.text: Suggest posting about it online to see who replies to her
options.then: A few strangers reply. None of them knows her.

options.text: Say she should ask another friend who had a similar problem once
options.then: The friend is worried too. Nobody trained is involved.

options.text: Suggest a trusted adult or Tele-MANAS 14416, and go with her
options.then: She nods slowly. "Okay. Can we go to the counsellor?"

steps.why: A trusted adult or Tele-MANAS 14416 brings trained support to something this heavy.

steps.prompt: Asha says she's scared of what her parents will think. What do you do?

options.text: Tell her parents yourself without asking her first
options.then: Asha is shocked and feels overruled. She needs time before she can talk with you again.

options.text: Say her parents will just panic, so skip telling them
options.then: She agrees, relieved. No adult is there for her.

options.text: Tell her to wait until she feels ready, however long that takes
options.then: She nods. Weeks pass, and the only help is still you.

options.text: Offer to be with her when she tells them
options.then: She breathes out. "If you're there, I can try."

steps.why: Being beside her when she tells an adult makes it easier to say, and it is never her fault.

scenarios.debrief: When a friend shares something this heavy, stay close and help them reach help.
scenarios.relearn: For serious distress, point them to Tele-MANAS 14416 or a trusted adult.

scenarios.hook: You want to ask your friend Hina to really be there for you this week.
scenarios.setup: She catches you at lunch.

steps.prompt: Hina says: "Hey, how've you been? Really."

options.text: "Honestly, rough. Could you check in on me?"
options.then: She puts down her tiffin. "Of course. I'm glad you said."

options.text: "Oh, you know. Busy with everything. You?"
options.then: "Totally," she says, but she studies your face. You don't say more.

options.text: "All good. Don't worry about me. I'm absolutely fine."
options.then: She smiles. "Okay!" and moves on to her day, though she glances back once.

options.text: "Same as always. What about you? How's your week going?"
options.then: She starts talking about herself, then stops. "Wait, you didn't really answer me."

steps.why: Saying you're rough and what you need is the clearest ask.

steps.prompt: Later Hina says: "I want to check in on you this week. How should I, texts or in person?"

options.text: "Never mind. You're busy too."
options.then: She protests, but you wave it off. She says she will text anyway.

options.text: "A message each evening, and a walk on Saturday."
options.then: "Perfect. I'll set a reminder."

options.text: "Whatever works for you. I'm easy."
options.then: She shrugs. "Okay, I'll see."

options.text: "Just message me if you remember."
options.then: She laughs. "I'll try." Nothing is fixed.

steps.why: A specific plan makes it easy for her to show up.

steps.prompt: A few evenings later Hina texts: "How are you tonight?"

options.text: "Fine!" Add a smiley and nothing else.
options.then: She sends a thumbs-up. The check-in turns into small talk.

options.text: "Don't worry. You've already done enough."
options.then: "Okay," she writes, and slows down.

options.text: Leave it on read until the morning
options.then: She tries again tomorrow, but the evening was lonely.

options.text: "Still heavy, but better for hearing from you."
options.then: She replies with a heart and a call request.

steps.why: Answering honestly keeps the check-ins useful.

steps.prompt: Hina says: "I've been thinking. Shall we see the school counsellor next week? I can come with you."

options.text: "I'll see how I feel then."
options.then: She says okay. The week fills up fast.

options.text: "Maybe you could ask the counsellor about it for me first."
options.then: She hesitates. "They'd want to hear from you, though." Nothing is booked.

options.text: "Yes. Let's go together on Monday."
options.then: She smiles. "I'll meet you after assembly."

options.text: "No, it's not that serious."
options.then: She nods, a bit unsure.

steps.why: Going together to a counsellor makes the next step easier, and needing help is not a failure.

scenarios.relearn: A simple, direct ask, 'could you check in on me?', opens real support.

scenarios.hook: A friend named Tanay has gone quiet and seems off, and you want to open the door.
scenarios.setup: You sit beside him at lunch.

steps.prompt: Tanay says in a low voice: "Hey. I'm just tired."

options.text: "Okay, rest up then!" Give him space and leave him be.
options.then: He nods. The tired look stays.

options.text: "You've seemed off lately. I'm here, no pressure."
options.then: He glances at you. "Thanks. I might take you up on that."

options.text: "Tired of what? Come on, tell me what is actually wrong."
options.then: He shifts. "It's nothing. Forget it."

options.text: "Same here. I'm tired of everything lately too, honestly."
options.then: He half-smiles. The talk turns to you.

steps.why: An open, no-pressure line lets him come to you when he is ready.

steps.prompt: A few days later Tanay says: "Everything feels heavy lately. I don't even know why."

options.text: "Have you tried exercise? It fixes everything."
options.then: He gives a small laugh. "Maybe."

options.text: "That sounds hard. I'm listening."
options.then: He exhales. "Thanks. I didn't want to burden anyone."

options.text: "Everyone feels that sometimes. You'll be fine."
options.then: He nods, but he stops talking.

options.text: "Let's get some chai and forget about it."
options.then: He comes along. The heaviness comes too.

steps.why: Listening first tells him it's safe to say more.

steps.prompt: Tanay says: "I don't want my parents to know. Can you keep this to yourself?"

options.text: "I can't keep this secret. Let's find an adult together."
options.then: He is quiet, then nods. "Okay. Together."

options.text: "Fine. But I'll tell a few friends to look out for you."
options.then: He feels exposed and goes quiet.

options.text: "Promise. This stays between you and me, I swear."
options.then: You carry it together, and it feels heavier every day.

options.text: "Okay. But you should tell them soon."
options.then: He agrees. A week later nothing has changed.

steps.why: Staying with him while an adult joins is how he gets help, and it is never his fault.

steps.prompt: Days later Tanay says: "It isn't getting lighter. Who else could I talk to?"

options.text: "Nobody. Maybe it will pass if we just wait a while."
options.then: He looks away. Another week goes by.

options.text: "Just tell your parents tonight, all by yourself, okay?"
options.then: He freezes. "I can't do that alone."

options.text: "The counsellor, or Tele-MANAS 14416. I'll come along."
options.then: He nods. "Can we go tomorrow?"

options.text: "A friend of mine went through this. I'll ask her."
options.then: She is kind, but she is not trained to help.

steps.why: A counsellor or Tele-MANAS 14416 brings trained support, and you can go along.

scenarios.relearn: A warm, no-pressure opener lets a struggling friend know support is there.

scenarios.hook: A senior has done the scholarship process you're lost in.
scenarios.setup: You catch Meghna after class.

steps.prompt: Meghna says: "Oh, hi! Need something?"

options.text: "It's fine. I'll figure the forms out somehow."
options.then: She says okay and heads off, then turns back. "You look stuck, though."

options.text: "Can you just send me your filled form to copy from?"
options.then: She hesitates. "That won't work. Your documents are different. But I can help."

options.text: "Nothing, really. I just wanted to say hi to you."
options.then: She waves, then pauses. "You looked like you needed something, though."

options.text: "You've done this before. Could you spare ten minutes?"
options.then: She smiles. "Sure. Walk with me."

steps.why: Asking for a small slice of time is a clear, strong move.

steps.prompt: Meghna says: "So, which part are you stuck on?"

options.text: "Nothing big. I'll ask you later if I really need to."
options.then: She nods. "Most people get stuck on the income certificate, though. Let's start there."

options.text: "Could you just fill the whole thing in for me instead?"
options.then: She frowns kindly. "I can show you, but you'll write it."

options.text: "Everything, honestly. I don't want to waste your time."
options.then: She waves it off, but now she has to guess your gaps.

options.text: "The income certificate. I don't know the steps."
options.then: "That's the tricky bit. I'll walk you through it."

steps.why: Naming exactly what you're stuck on lets her help well.

steps.prompt: Meghna says: "You'll need a certificate from the office. Do you know who to ask?"

options.text: "I'll ask whoever is at the desk."
options.then: The wrong person sends you to a queue.

options.text: "No. Could you tell me who, and what to say?"
options.then: She writes a name and two lines to say.

options.text: "I'll ask my friend to do it for me."
options.then: He agrees. He isn't sure what to say.

options.text: "I'll skip it. It sounds like too much."
options.then: She looks concerned. "Don't skip it. Let's find a way."

steps.why: Asking for the name and the words turns a wall into a step.

steps.prompt: Meghna says: "Let me know how it goes. Pay it forward later, okay?"

options.text: "Sure. Whatever you say, honestly."
options.then: She frowns, unsure whether you mean it.

options.text: "I'll try, but I don't like asking people."
options.then: She nods. "It gets easier. Ask me again."

options.text: "Don't worry. I won't bother you again after this."
options.then: She shakes her head. "That's not what I meant."

options.text: "I will. Thank you. I'll tell you how it goes."
options.then: She grins. "I'll be waiting."

steps.why: Asking someone who has done it before is a strength, and you can do the same for others later.

scenarios.relearn: Asking someone who's done it before is a strength, not a failure.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Yash has strong ideas about who needs counselling.
scenarios.setup: You answer him.

steps.prompt: Yash says: "Counselling is for people who can't cope. Not us."

options.text: "Mm." Shrug and look down at your phone
options.then: He takes your silence as agreement.

options.text: "Ha, true!" Laugh along so it isn't awkward.
options.then: He grins. The joke stands.

options.text: "It's like a doctor for your mind. That's smart."
options.then: He tilts his head. "Hm. When you say it like that."

options.text: "That's a really stupid thing to say, Yash. Grow up."
options.then: He bristles. "Wow. Okay, relax."

steps.why: Saying it calmly corrects the myth without a fight.

steps.prompt: Yash says: "Honestly, if I went, people would think I'm weak."

options.text: "I think it takes courage. Would you call a friend weak?"
options.then: He thinks. "No. I'd say he's brave."

options.text: "You're right. People would talk about it for weeks."
options.then: He shrugs. The idea of going feels closed for good.

options.text: "Yeah, so don't go. Just keep it all to yourself, na."
options.then: He nods. The idea gets buried.

options.text: "True. Just watch some videos online and sort it out yourself."
options.then: He nods. The videos don't help, and he still has no one to talk to.

steps.why: Reaching for support is strong, and stigma is the only thing that says otherwise.

steps.prompt: Yash says: "Say someone did want to go, though. How would they even start?"

options.text: "Talk to a trusted adult or the counsellor. Tele-MANAS 14416 too."
options.then: He nods. "That sounds doable."

options.text: "Just search for a therapist online and pick the first one."
options.then: He nods, but he has no idea whom to trust.

options.text: "You don't need to do that. Just sleep more and relax."
options.then: He laughs. The heavy part stays.

options.text: "I don't really know. Ask someone else about it."
options.then: He shrugs and drops it.

steps.why: A trusted adult, the school counsellor or Tele-MANAS 14416 are real first steps.

steps.prompt: Yash says: "A friend of mine has been really down. Should I say something?"

options.text: "No. It's not your business, so stay out of it."
options.then: He nods. The friend stays on his own.

options.text: "Wait until he brings it up himself, then see."
options.then: He nods, and the friend waits too.

options.text: "Tell his parents first, without telling him."
options.then: He is unsure. His friend might feel surprised, with no say in it.

options.text: "Yes. Say you care, and offer to find a trusted adult together."
options.then: He nods. "I'll talk to him tomorrow. Maybe the counsellor can help."

steps.why: Caring and bringing in a trusted adult together shows that reaching out is normal.

scenarios.relearn: Reaching out for mental-health support is normal, smart and strong.

scenarios.hook: You are moving to another city and want to keep a close friend close.
scenarios.setup: The night before you leave, you sit with Alisha.

steps.prompt: Alisha says: "I can't believe you're going. What if we drift apart?"

options.text: "Honestly, people do drift apart. It happens a lot."
options.then: She looks down. "I know. I just hoped we wouldn't."

options.text: "We won't drift apart. Don't be silly about it."
options.then: She smiles, but her eyes stay worried.

options.text: "Distance won't change us if we make time. Weekly calls?"
options.then: She sniffs and smiles. "Yes. Let's do that."

options.text: "I guess we'll just see how it goes for us."
options.then: She nods quietly. The quiet is its own answer.

steps.why: A concrete plan helps a friendship survive distance.

steps.prompt: Alisha says: "I do want to stay in touch, though. Should we fix a regular day? I have tuition on Sundays."

options.text: "Whatever day you like. I'm easy."
options.then: "Okay, I'll see," she says. The plan floats.

options.text: "Saturday evening works. We'll swap if it's off."
options.then: She laughs. "Done."

options.text: "Sunday morning. Skip tuition."
options.then: She stiffens. "I can't."

options.text: "Let's skip the schedule. We'll message randomly."
options.then: She shrugs. Random becomes rare.

steps.why: A fixed day, with room to swap, makes the habit last.

steps.prompt: Two weeks later Alisha texts: "I haven't called or messaged in days. I forgot. Sorry!"

options.text: "It's fine. We probably need less contact anyway."
options.then: She replies "oh". The call frequency drops.

options.text: "No problem. I'll message you when I'm free."
options.then: She says okay. A week goes by with no message.

options.text: "You forgot? Seriously? I made time for you."
options.then: She feels awful. The next call starts stiffly.

options.text: "No worries. Let's talk tomorrow evening."
options.then: She sends a heart. "Tomorrow!"

steps.why: Rescheduling kindly keeps the habit going without blame.

steps.prompt: Alisha says: "You sound tired. How are you finding it there?"

options.text: "Great! Everything is perfect here."
options.then: She wants to believe you. The distance grows.

options.text: "Fine. I've made lots of friends."
options.then: She lets it go. She senses it isn't the whole story.

options.text: "Don't worry about me. Tell me about you."
options.then: She talks for an hour. You feel more alone.

options.text: "Lonely some days. Can we talk longer next time?"
options.then: She says, "Of course. I was hoping you'd say so."

steps.why: Being honest about the hard days is how close friends stay close.

scenarios.relearn: Build your support network before you need it; keep close bonds through change.

scenarios.hook: Your friend Pia offers to help with a project, and you usually wave her off.
scenarios.setup: She puts her bag down beside you.

steps.prompt: Pia says: "You look swamped. Let me help."

options.text: "It's fine. I'm used to doing it alone."
options.then: She nods slowly but doesn't leave. You're just as swamped as before.

options.text: "Maybe later. Not right now, I'm a bit busy."
options.then: She says okay and stays nearby. You are no less swamped.

options.text: "Yes, please. Thank you. I could use that."
options.then: She smiles. "Good. Move over."

options.text: "No no, I've got it. Don't trouble yourself."
options.then: She shrugs. "Okay. Shout if you change your mind." She stays nearby.

steps.why: Saying yes lets her help, and it's how connection works.

steps.prompt: Pia says: "So, what's the hardest part for you?"

options.text: "Nothing, really. I just wanted some company here."
options.then: She laughs. The data section stays untouched.

options.text: "Just take it and do it all for me, please."
options.then: She laughs, then realises you're serious.

options.text: "Everything. I should have started way earlier."
options.then: She pauses. "It's not about blame. Pick one part."

options.text: "The data section. Could you check it with me?"
options.then: She scans it. "Easy. Let's split it."

steps.why: Naming one hard part gives her a real task to take on.

steps.prompt: Pia says: "You seem stressed in general. Anything else I can do?"

options.text: "I'll tell you if I need more."
options.then: She nods. You probably won't tell her.

options.text: "Could we study together twice a week?"
options.then: She grins. "Yes. Tuesday and Friday?"

options.text: "No, you've already done so much."
options.then: She says okay, a little disappointed.

options.text: "Just stay nearby. You don't have to do anything."
options.then: She stays. She can't tell if she is helping.

steps.why: A specific, regular ask lets her keep supporting you.

steps.prompt: Pia says: "Next time you're swamped, tell me sooner. Will you?"

options.text: "Yes. And I'll help when you're swamped too."
options.then: She grins. "Deal."

options.text: "Sure. If I remember it when I'm swamped."
options.then: She laughs, unsure if you mean it.

options.text: "I'll try not to need it, Pia. Really."
options.then: She raises an eyebrow. "That's not the point."

options.text: "Maybe. I just don't like asking people for help."
options.then: She nods. "I'll keep asking you, then."

steps.why: Being open to help, and offering it back, keeps support going both ways.

scenarios.relearn: Letting people support you isn't a burden; it's how connection works.

scenarios.hook: Aunty's advice about your future is really pressure, and you want to hold your line warmly.
scenarios.setup: She corners you after lunch at a family function.

steps.prompt: Aunty says: "Take the course my friend's son did. That's the sensible path."

options.text: "Okay, Aunty. You know best about this."
options.then: She beams and keeps going. Something in you sinks.

options.text: "It's my life, so please stay out of it."
options.then: Her face hardens. The room gets quiet.

options.text: "I'll think about it." Then plan to say nothing more.
options.then: She takes that as a yes and tells your mother.

options.text: "I hear you. I'm deciding by what matters to me."
options.then: She blinks. "Hm. Well, think about it."

steps.why: Warmth plus a clear line keeps the relationship and your choice.

steps.prompt: Aunty adds: "Your parents agree with me, you know. They want what's best for you."

options.text: "They're wrong too, and honestly so are you, Aunty."
options.then: She gasps. "Such language!"

options.text: "Then I guess I must be wrong about all of it."
options.then: She smiles. You doubt yourself.

options.text: "I'll talk to them myself and share how I'm deciding."
options.then: She nods, caught off guard. "Fine. You do that."

options.text: "I won't talk about it. Ask someone else."
options.then: She huffs and falls silent, then circles back. "Someone has to talk sense into you."

steps.why: Speaking to your parents yourself keeps your voice in the conversation.

steps.prompt: Aunty says: "You're young. You don't know what's good for you."

options.text: "Exactly. So let's just drop this whole topic."
options.then: She says okay. The pressure stays in the air.

options.text: "Maybe you're right. I'm probably just too young."
options.then: She nods, pleased. You feel smaller.

options.text: "Don't call me young. I'm almost an adult."
options.then: She laughs. "Almost. Exactly."

options.text: "I'm still learning, and I'm deciding by what matters to me."
options.then: She softens. "Hm. That's sensible."

steps.why: Admitting you are still learning while holding your values shows maturity, not weakness.

steps.prompt: After a pause Aunty asks: "So what are you thinking of studying?"

options.text: "Sure. Here's what I'm considering and why."
options.then: She listens. "Hm. Interesting. Tell me more."

options.text: "I'd rather not say. Please stop asking me about this."
options.then: She nods. The question follows you to the next function.

options.text: "Whatever you want it to be, Aunty. Honestly."
options.then: She smiles. You feel hollow.

options.text: "Why do you want to know? So you can argue about it?"
options.then: She stiffens. "I'm only asking."

steps.why: Sharing your thinking keeps the door open without giving up your choice.

scenarios.relearn: Real support backs your own values; you can hold a boundary warmly.
